novelty_flags.label: thm:adaptive-oracle
novelty_flags.one_line: The survey omits Zeng et al. (2026), the closest current result on outcome-history-adaptive sequential switchback assignment; its no/first-order-carryover scope is orthogonal but must be compared against the claimed policy-uniform no-gain oracle.

novelty_flags.one_line: The promise table calls BojinovSimchiLeviZhao2023 and YuMaLiu2025 strict tightenings, but no solve target states a formal strict inclusion, separation, or oracle comparison against either published result.

soundness_flags.label: ass:polynomial-envelope and prop:no-carryover-reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: Because the envelope sums only lags ell>=1, two paths differing only in z_t must have identical Y_t, so the main class forbids direct treatment effects whereas ass:no-carryover permits them; Proposition 1 is not a reduction of the polynomial model.

source_verification_receipts.version: Management Science 69(7), July 2023 issue; publisher citation metadata
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and article-information page, lines 257-262 and 279-303
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article derives a minimax discrete optimization design under assumptions on carryover order, studies misspecification, and provides a data-driven order-identification procedure.
The paper proposes a multi-unit minimax design with spillover and carryover effects, Horvitz--Thompson inference, and carryover-order misspecification analysis.
The cited version studies Markovian systems with geometric mixing, reports T^{-1/3} error for standard switchbacks and a burn-in improvement of order sqrt(log(T)/T).
The paper studies graph-based spatial interference and hidden-Markov temporal interference, with a clustered switchback truncated-exposure Horvitz--Thompson estimator and near-parametric MSE.
The paper estimates a steady-state reward difference between unknown Markov chains and constructs a consistent, asymptotically efficient adaptive online design under its Markov/MLE model.

source_verification_receipts.version: Preprint corresponding to Annals of Statistics 39(3), 1608-1632 (2011)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops a kernel-estimator selection rule with L_s-risk oracle inequalities and adaptive minimaxity over anisotropic Nikol'skii classes.
The paper proves a constrained-risk inequality for arbitrary non-decreasing losses and explicitly motivates adaptive-estimation lower bounds.
The paper tests whether a specified finite influence-period bound is underestimated by comparing estimators with different lag assumptions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the envelope by including a lag-zero/direct-effect term or by restricting its comparison to paths with z_t=z'_t; then make the no-carryover proposition a literal special-case reduction and recompute the rate.
Add Zeng et al. (2026) and state a dedicated comparison theorem showing exactly why the polynomial-envelope all-sequential-policy lower bound is outside its no/first-order-carryover setting.

Replace the comparator-table assertion with a formal strict-extension statement: identify the finite-order subclasses corresponding to each named comparator and prove the common-design oracle guarantee is unavailable from their specified-order results.
Specify the multiscale allocation, positivity probabilities, and selection penalty sufficiently to support a policy-uniform lower-bound construction and an implementable upper-bound design.
Correct bibliography metadata: Bojinov--Simchi-Levi--Zhao is Management Science 69(7):3759-3777, and Duchi--Ruan is PMLR 130:802-810 rather than PMLR 134:1-30.
